population.span: We performed a randomized, double-blind trial involving patients recruited within 30 days after a myocardial infarction.

endpoint.span: The primary efficacy end point was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, resuscitated cardiac arrest, myocardial infarction, stroke, or urgent hospitalization for angina leading to coronary revascularization.

estimate.span: The primary end point occurred in 5.5% of the patients in the colchicine group, as compared with 7.1% of those in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.77; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.61 to 0.96; P = 0.02).

ci.span: The primary end point occurred in 5.5% of the patients in the colchicine group, as compared with 7.1% of those in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.77; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.61 to 0.96; P = 0.02).

treatment_strategy.span: The patients were randomly assigned to receive either low-dose colchicine (0.5 mg once daily) or placebo.

follow_up.span: Patients were followed for a median of 22.6 months.

absent_reason.analysis_set: Neither abstract explicitly states the analysis set, and the registry result population is blank. Randomization and arm denominators do not establish an intention-to-treat analysis.

entry_population_matches_question.why: Registry eligibility specifies adults with acute myocardial infarction within the preceding 30 days; the served intention-to-treat designation remains unverified.
entry_population_matches_question.span: Inclusion Criteria: * Males and females of at least 18 years of age capable and willing to provide informed consent * Patient must have suffered a documented acute myocardial infarction within the last 30 days

notes: The served HR and confidence interval match the primary composite in the abstract. Registry evidence supports adult eligibility. Follow-up is reported as a median, not a fixed endpoint timepoint. BOUND does not establish the served intention-to-treat analysis-set claim.
